speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are suffering from chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to help me understand your condition, how long have these symptoms been persisting?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Campylobacter jejuni infection (likely post-infectious Irritable Bowel Syndrome).

The patient reports a history of camping and a sick contact, which strongly suggests a food or waterborne pathogen like Campylobacter. Given the chronic nature (4 months), mucus discharge, urgency, and relief of pain with defecation, this is highly suggestive of post-infectious Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS-D) or a chronic infectious etiology.

REQUEST TEST: Stool Culture and Ova & Parasites.
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal CT_Scan (to rule out structural causes if symptoms persist).
